guideTitle: The Best Portable Docking Stations for Working From Anywhere
metaTitle: Best Portable Docking Stations for Remote Work (2026)
metaDescription: We compared travel hubs and powered docks for remote work on size, display outputs, power pass-through, Ethernet and card readers, from pocket hubs to an all-day desk dock.
introParagraphs: A remote worker's dock often has two jobs: sit on a home desk running monitors, and travel to a hotel, café or co-working desk. Small hubs that draw power from the laptop are easy to carry; powered docks with their own adapter can charge the laptop and run more, but they are bigger and stay put.

Whatever you choose, how many monitors you can run depends on your laptop. Many laptops, including base Apple M-series models, support only one or two external displays over USB-C, and a hub's dual HDMI may mirror rather than extend. Check your laptop's documentation first.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, port configurations, power design and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $27 to $170 at the time of writing.

ugreen-10-in-1-revodok-pro-210.summary: A compact 10-in-1 hub with HDMI, 100W pass-through, Ethernet and an SD/TF reader.
ugreen-10-in-1-revodok-pro-210.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Pro 210 is the sensible all-rounder for travel and home: a compact 10-in-1 hub with HDMI (listed for dual 4K 60Hz or a single 8K 30Hz display), 100W power pass-through, gigabit Ethernet, 5Gbps USB-C and USB-A, and an SD/TF reader.

It needs no power brick of its own, so it is light for a daily bag, and wired Ethernet is useful where hotel or café Wi-Fi is unreliable.

To charge the laptop you plug your own charger into its pass-through port. Dual-display support depends on your laptop.
cons: Needs your own charger for pass-through
ugreen-10-in-1-revodok-pro-210.bestFor: Remote workers who want one light hub for home and travel.
ugreen-10-in-1-revodok-pro-210.skipIf: You want the dock to charge the laptop by itself; the Anker Prime or HP Dock G5 have their own power.

anker-prime-14-port-160w.summary: A 14-port dock with its own 160W power supply, dual 4K support and 10Gbps data.
anker-prime-14-port-160w.description:
The Anker Prime is the pick for a fixed home or co-working desk: a 14-port dock with its own 160W power supply, so it can charge the laptop while running two 4K displays and peripherals.

It adds 10Gbps data, audio and Ethernet ports, and a small display showing real-time status.

It is the most expensive dock here at the time of writing and too bulky for daily carrying.
pros: Charges the laptop on its own
anker-prime-14-port-160w.bestFor: A permanent desk that one cable should fully power.
anker-prime-14-port-160w.skipIf: You carry your dock daily; a UGREEN or Anker Nano hub is lighter.

hp-usb-c-dock-g5.summary: HP's powered 11-in-1 business dock for USB-C and Thunderbolt laptops.
hp-usb-c-dock-g5.description:
The HP USB-C Dock G5 is the choice if you work on a company-issued laptop: a powered 11-in-1 business dock that HP lists for both USB-C and Thunderbolt laptops, with charging, networking and data in one unit.

HP designs it with managed business environments in mind, and a business-brand dock may be easier to get approved by an IT department. Check with IT before buying any dock for a managed laptop.

It needs an outlet and costs more than the travel hubs.
hp-usb-c-dock-g5.skipIf: You need something to carry; a travel hub is lighter.

ugreen-7-in-1-revodok-pro.summary: A 7-in-1 aluminum hub with HDMI, 10Gbps data and 100W pass-through for about $27.
ugreen-7-in-1-revodok-pro.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Pro 7-in-1 is the lowest-priced hub here: an aluminum 7-in-1 with HDMI listed for dual 4K 60Hz, 10Gbps USB-A and USB-C data, and 100W power pass-through.

Aluminum should shed heat better than plastic, and it is small enough to live in a laptop bag.

It has no SD reader or Ethernet, and dual-display support depends on your laptop.
ugreen-7-in-1-revodok-pro.bestFor: Budget travelers who need a monitor and fast USB.
ugreen-7-in-1-revodok-pro.skipIf: You need Ethernet; the Revodok Pro 210 has it.

anker-nano-8-in-1.summary: A pocket-size 8-in-1 hub with 4K HDMI, 10Gbps USB-C, SD/TF and 85W pass-through.
anker-nano-8-in-1.description:
The Anker Nano is the smallest hub here, for minimalist travel: 4K 60Hz HDMI, a 10Gbps USB-C port, two USB-A ports, an SD/TF reader and 85W pass-through.

It is small enough to pocket.

It supports a single external display, and 85W pass-through may not keep up with higher-power laptops.
anker-nano-8-in-1.bestFor: Travelers who want the smallest hub for one monitor.
anker-nano-8-in-1.skipIf: You need Ethernet; the Revodok Pro 210 includes it.

anker-13-in-1-triple-display.summary: A 13-in-1 dock with two HDMI and one DisplayPort for up to three displays.
anker-13-in-1-triple-display.description:
The Anker 13-in-1 is the dock for a multi-monitor setup: two HDMI ports and a DisplayPort for up to three displays, plus 10Gbps USB-C, 5Gbps USB-A, Ethernet, audio and an SD reader, with 85W charging.

Anker lists compatibility with Dell, HP and Lenovo laptops. Triple display depends on your laptop supporting it.

It is bulkier than the travel hubs. If you connect to a hotel TV, protected streaming content may not play over any dock, depending on the TV and app.
specs: Displays: 2 x HDMI, 1 x DisplayPort (up to 3, laptop-dependent)
anker-13-in-1-triple-display.bestFor: Desks, or co-working spaces, where you connect several monitors.
anker-13-in-1-triple-display.skipIf: You only use one monitor; a travel hub is smaller and cheaper.

anker-8-in-1-85w.summary: An 8-in-1 hub with dual HDMI, gigabit Ethernet, SD and 85W pass-through.
anker-8-in-1-85w.description:
The Anker 8-in-1 sits between the travel hubs and the larger docks: two HDMI outputs, gigabit Ethernet, 85W power delivery and an SD reader in a compact shell.

Wired Ethernet helps with video calls on unreliable Wi-Fi.

A charger is not included, the listing does not state USB-A speed (check it if you use a 4K webcam), and dual display depends on your laptop.
anker-8-in-1-85w.bestFor: Remote workers who want Ethernet and HDMI in a small hub.
anker-8-in-1-85w.skipIf: You want 100W pass-through; the UGREEN hubs list it.

ugreen-14-in-1-multiport.badge: Most Ports Without a Power Brick
ugreen-14-in-1-multiport.summary: A 14-in-1 bus-powered adapter with dual HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet and 100W pass-through.
ugreen-14-in-1-multiport.description:
This 14-in-1 adapter packs the most ports into a hub without its own power supply: two HDMI ports and a DisplayPort, gigabit Ethernet, four USB-A and two USB-C ports, a 100W pass-through port, an SD/TF reader and audio.

It is a full desk setup that still fits in a bag.

To charge the laptop you need to plug a charger into it; without one, everything runs from the laptop's battery. It is bulkier than the nano hubs.
pros: Most ports in a brick-free hub
cons: Runs from laptop battery unless you add a charger
ugreen-14-in-1-multiport.bestFor: Remote workers who want a full port set in a portable hub.
ugreen-14-in-1-multiport.skipIf: You travel light; the Anker Nano or UGREEN 7-in-1 are smaller.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Bus-powered hubs are small and need your laptop charger plugged into them to charge the laptop. Powered docks (Anker Prime, HP Dock G5) have their own supply.
Hubs listing two or three outputs rely on the laptop. Check its maximum external displays over USB-C; some laptops mirror rather than extend.
Compare with your laptop charger. 85W suits many ultrabooks; 100W leaves more headroom.
Wired Ethernet helps calls on poor Wi-Fi; a card reader helps anyone moving photos or video.
The Anker Nano and UGREEN 7-in-1 are the easiest to carry; the Anker Prime and HP are desk-only.

faq.q: What's the difference between a bus-powered hub and a powered dock?
faq.a: A bus-powered hub takes power from the laptop and can pass through power from your charger. A powered dock has its own supply and can charge the laptop directly, but it is larger.

faq.q: Will a dock work with a hotel TV?
faq.a: Usually for showing your screen over HDMI. Some streaming apps may block protected content on external displays, depending on the TV and app.

faq.q: Can I use a hub at a café without an outlet?
faq.a: Yes, but everything runs from your laptop battery, so it will drain faster than working plugged in.

faq.q: Why does my webcam look worse through a hub?
faq.a: Some hub USB-A ports are slower than a laptop's own ports. Check the port speed, or connect a high-resolution webcam directly to the laptop.

faq.q: Which dock suits a corporate laptop?
faq.a: The HP USB-C Dock G5 is designed for business use. Check with your IT department before connecting any dock to a managed laptop.

bottomLine: For most remote workers, the UGREEN Revodok Pro 210 covers home and travel in one light hub with Ethernet and a card reader. The Anker Nano and UGREEN 7-in-1 are the smaller, cheaper travel options, and the 14-in-1 fits the most ports in a hub without a brick.

For a fixed desk, the Anker Prime is worth paying more for as a one-cable dock with its own power, the HP Dock G5 suits company laptops, and the Anker 13-in-1 is the choice for multiple monitors, provided your laptop supports them.
